rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must include required form and information
rules.requirement: When a landlord gives a notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant, it must be accompanied by a form that includes documentation of any repayment agreements and information about rental assistance programs, trial court rules, and legal restrictions on evictions. The form must prominently display a statement that the notice is not an eviction and that the tenant is entitled to a legal proceeding.
rules.quotedSpan: A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter shall be accompanied by a form that shall include, but not be limited to: (i) documentation of any agreements between the tenant and landlord for the tenant to repay the landlord for nonpayment of rent; and (ii) information on: (1) rental assistance programs including, but not limited to, the residential assistance for families in transition program; (2) applicable trial court rules, standing orders or emergency administrative orders pertaining to actions for summary process; and (3) any relevant federal or state legal restrictions on residential evictions.
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental housing in Massachusetts
warnings: The statute requires a form to accompany notice to quit for nonpayment, but does not specify an effective date. The retrieval date is 2026-10-01, so the rule is assumed to be in force as of that date.
The statute does not define exemptions based on building characteristics; coverage is assumed to be all residential rental units.

M.G.L. c. 186 § 31 addresses procedural requirements for eviction notices (notice to quit for nonpayment) and does not establish substantive rules in the six tracked categories (rent increase limits, just-cause eviction grounds, security deposits, application/screening fees, screening restrictions, or algorithmic rent setting). The rule recorded here relates to just-cause eviction only in the narrow sense that it requires certain notices and information when a landlord issues a notice to quit, but it does not define the grounds or reasons for which eviction is permissible or prohibited.
